_about: Datasheet-verified pin functions and the connection rules the datasheets state as requirements. Checked by verify_release.py --only pins so the verification does not have to be repeated by hand. Every entry cites the document and revision it came from; re-verify against a newer revision before trusting it for a new order.

U1.source: Diodes DS41326 Rev. 3-2 (Nov 2024), Pin Descriptions + Typical Application Circuit
U1.notes: Fixed 5.0 V output, so FB connects straight to the output node with no divider (the divider is only for the adjustable AP63200/AP63201). EN tied to VIN is explicitly sanctioned: 'Attach to VIN or leave open for automatic startup'.

rules.why: EN tied to VIN for always-on operation

U3.source: Diodes DS41326 Rev. 3-2 (Nov 2024), Pin Descriptions + Setting the Output Voltage
U3.notes: Fixed 3.3 V output; same FB-direct-to-output rule as U1. VIN minimum is 3.8 V, which SYS_5V clears even from a weak USB source.

rules.why: EN tied to VIN for always-on operation

U6.source: TI SLVSE71 (Sept 2017), Pin Functions + Electrical Characteristics
U6.notes: Adjustable, so VFB needs the external divider that R28/R29 provide. EN carries an internal 120-400 kOhm pull-down to ground (245 kOhm typical), which must be included when sizing the enable network: with R26 10k in series and R27 100k to ground a 3.3 V GPIO still presents 2.79-2.93 V against a 1.6 V threshold, and the pin sits at 0 V when the GPIO is low or high-Z.

Q1.source: Alpha & Omega AO4407A Rev. 11.1 (March 2024), SOIC-8 pin configuration
Q1.notes: P-channel. For reverse-polarity protection the drain faces the battery and the source faces the load, so the body diode conducts in normal polarity and blocks when the pack is reversed; the gate is pulled to ground through R1 and clamped by D2.

rules.why: all source pins are one terminal
all drain pins are one terminal

U5.source: NXP PN7160_PN7161 product data sheet Rev. 3.2 (30 Sept 2021), Table 5 pin description
U5.notes: Pins 23/24 (ANT1/ANT2) and 25 (VDD(HF)) are the very low-power RF field detector of data sheet section 10.4.4: an internal rectifier that lets the controller notice an external field while powered off. A HomeKey lock is the reader and must poll actively, so that block is deliberately unpopulated and all three pins stay open. Pin 39 WKUP_REQ carries a 55-120 kOhm internal pull-down in Hard Power Down, so leaving it open is defined rather than floating. The project symbol labels pin 37 DCDC_EN; the data sheet calls it i.c. on HVQFN40. The connection (open) is right either way, but the name is not the vendor's.

rules.why: data sheet: VSS(PAD), VSS(A), VSS(TX) and the centre pad must be connected to ground
data sheet: TVDD_IN and TVDD_IN2 must be connected to VDD(TX)
data sheet: VDD(A) connects to VDD(D), and VDD must be connected to both
data sheet: VBAT2 must be connected to VBAT
VDD(UP) is the TXLDO input; this design feeds it from the same rail as VBAT
data sheet: i.c. pins are to be left open
very low-power RF field detector deliberately unpopulated: a HomeKey lock polls, it is not woken by an external field
